quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, even if traffic lights say otherwise.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, turns and curves are especially dangerous. Slow down more than you normally would when taking turns on wet or slick surfaces.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving immediately.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see ahead clearly, if oncoming traffic is in the passing lane, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, or on a bridge. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and reduce visibility. You must use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road surface is slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, always signal 100 feet in advance. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and proper inflation. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid on turns. Keep tires in good condition, reduce your speed, avoid cruise control, and watch for water or puddles.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as if they were thinking clearly.
Can drive faster because their senses are heightened.
Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Emotions like worry, anger, or sadness distract you from driving. Your mind focuses on other things instead of the road. Take time to calm down before you drive.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to traffic already on the road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (for example, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol weakens your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: A driver taking over-the-counter medication should:

options.text: Continue to drive despite warning labels.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications, even cold or allergy remedies, can affect your driving. Always check the label for warnings. If unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with seat belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:

options.text: All occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object and injure others in the vehicle during a crash.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a standard crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can hear if a train is approaching.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (orange in work areas). They warn you of hazards or places where special rules apply.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill slope than smaller vehicles.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill slope than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road carefully and park as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done exiting the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: See a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when you think a driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child is running into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: When a drawbridge signal is red, you should:

options.text: Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.explanation: A red drawbridge signal means come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. The bridge is operating and the road is closed to all traffic.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
There is a stop sign at the crossing.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They tell drivers about road conditions and guide them safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and medicine together can increase how much they affect you. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signals whenever you move left or right. Signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: Following too closely means you may not have enough time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops. This can cause a collision.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: This sign is used to prevent:

options.text: Entrance from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entrance from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic only goes one way. You must not enter from your current direction.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection cross first. You can continue driving, but stay ready to slow down if the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find a different route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross the tracks. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: While backing out of your driveway.

questions.explanation: Before you start driving, make sure all your equipment works. Before starting your engine, adjust all mirrors so you can use them without leaning forward or backward.

questions.question: Which sign may show a driver is drunk?

options.text: They drive slower than other traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than other traffic, making jerking motions, and making quick, sudden stops.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Do not stop or back up on the highway, swerve across multiple lanes at the last second, or cross the median to turn around. All of these actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved in a traffic study.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a blind person who is using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions greatly affect your driving ability. You may not drive well if you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad. Stress reduces your ability to concentrate on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive while emotionally upset.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: To turn safely, use your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious traffic safety problem. You cannot drive safely when you drink alcohol or take drugs. Driving under the influence is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with drugs?

options.text: It decreases the effects of both.
It increases the effects of both.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous to combine them.
